data.narrative:
nTop, a Series C robotics and manufacturing software company founded by Bradley Rothenberg and Greg Schroy, has raised $138.9M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine comparables spanning robotics and manufacturing—one public (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private firms including Exotec, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Hadrian at stages ranging from Series B to Series D.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $139M total raised proxy, implying a valuation of $236M. Peer-median analysis across seven same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B. The peer set includes Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D).

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $201M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $943M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty regarding nTop's revenue scale, unit economics, and competitive positioning relative to the peer set. Stage-progression yields a more conservative floor given reliance on historical capital rather than revenue or market multiples. Peer-median analysis better captures sector dynamics but is sensitive to which comparables are deemed truly analogous. Additional clarity on revenue, growth rate, and gross margin would narrow the range materially.
